newsitem.title: BELGIUM: IFPI files complaint about bootleg CDs from Luxembourg.
newsitem.headline: IFPI files complaint about bootleg CDs from Luxembourg.

text.p: The European Commission has been asked to take legal proceedings against Luxembourg for failing to halt the flow of bootleg compact discs through the Grand Duchy.

The International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) said on Tuesday it had filed a complaint under European Union single market rules, saying Luxembourg has failed to enforce international copyright laws.
The IFPI -- which represents over 1,200 record producers worldwide -- said in a statement that over one million bootleg CDs entered the European Union through Luxembourg each year.
This was costing the music industry some $2.1 billion a year -- 20 percent of it in the EU.

The IFPI said most of the illegal CDs originated in Israel, the Czech Republic or the Far East. Once they had entered the customs-free EU, they were distributed throughout the 15-nation bloc but chiefly in Germany, Italy and Britain.
The complaint by the IFPI, formally lodged at the beginning of September, is the first taken by the recording industry against an EU state.
The Commission has already opened infringement proceedings against Luxembourg for failing to notify that it was enforcing two directives regarding copyright infringement.
But the IFPI complaint would step up the process as it would not only require notification, but also full and correct implementation.
